title: I Took the Church Nursery Sign-In Sheet to the Pastor's Wife

parts.text: I signed my toddler in at 9:55 with the code-word sticker the nursery required. The pastor's wife, June, walked past the desk with two grandchildren and no stickers. I was thirty, volunteer clipboard in my hand because I was on rotation. The policy on the half-door said every child, every week, no exceptions for staff families. A new volunteer looked at me. June said, "We know our own." Then a grandchild ran toward the parking lot because nobody had written a pickup code.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The grandchild is heading for the lot without a code because knowing your own is not a door.

social.video_title: Staff family skipped the nursery stickers — Part 1/2
social.description: Code-word policy, clipboard rotation, grandchildren without ink. Then a parking lot. Would you have left the desk?

parts.text: I stepped to the lot, picked up the child, and brought them back to the half-door. I asked June to sign the sheet. She did, red. The pastor later thanked me in a way that sounded like a meeting. The policy got a second copy at adult eye level. Stickers went on every shirt. My toddler ate goldfish. The lot stayed a lot. Knowing your own now includes writing it down, which is how knowing survives a busy Sunday.

social.video_title: The pickup code went on the grandchild after the lot — Part 2/2
social.description: Sheet signed in red, stickers for all shirts, goldfish as usual. Was family a fire code?
